purpose: Read-only official-document audit, not inference, database access or a production probe. Tests never fetch these sources.

sources.observation: Links to the Academic Reading multiple-choice-more-than-one-answer answer key.
Two required responses occupy two numbered questions in each pair. This is not a specification of every electronic multi-select scoring algorithm.

sources.excerpt: The IELTS Reading test contains 40 questions. Each correct answer is awarded 1 mark.
sources.observation: Supports one mark per numbered correct answer, not a universal partial-credit rule for a Langfens Question row containing a set.

excerpts: Not every paragraph (or section) may be used and some paragraphs (or sections) may be used more than once.
When the paragraphs (or sections) may be used more than once, the instructions will say: ‘You may choose any paragraph (or section) more than once’.
Number of sections: 3; the total text length is 2150–2750 words
sources.observation: Reuse permission is not a requirement that a generated key must repeat a letter.

limits: Hashes identify bytes retrieved for this audit; URLs may later change. Only short excerpts are retained in-repository; raw downloads were held under /tmp. The example and general scoring text do not prove a universal K-of-N subset-credit algorithm or penalization rule.
